frequency_question: How often do major U.S. debt/liquidity intervention programs reach high-volume scale targets within their initial multi-year implementation window?
membership_rule: Members include formal U.S. Treasury or Federal Reserve programs created to manage debt structure, liquidity, or repo/buyback dynamics that set target operational expansion paths. Excluded are one-off emergency crisis bailouts without multi-year operational targets.

cases.name: Federal Reserve Permanent Open Market Operations (POMO) Treasury purchase scale-up (2011-2012)
Federal Reserve Reverse Repo Operations (ON RRP) scaling phase (2021-2022)

coverage_note: 3 named; represents the universe of comparable discretionary U.S. structural debt/liquidity intervention scaling programs of this type.
known_gaps: Excludes minor tactical fine-tuning operations that did not feature explicit large-scale structural volume targets.
skeleton: Three distinct historical debt management or liquidity operation scaling cycles since 2000, where program volumes were either expanded to meet structural demand or curtailed due to changing fiscal conditions.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 3 relevant historical scaling attempts
validity_reason: Treasury debt management frameworks evolve slowly across structural regimes; this frequency remains valid through the current debt issuance architecture era.
